title: Neil's difficult summer job in Canada 🫛 | Practise your listening with Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hello Neil.
Hi Georgie. How are you?
I'm very well, thank you. How are you?
I'm excellent, thank you.
Good. Neil, have you ever had a bad or difficult job?
sentences.ko: 좋아. 닐, 힘들거나 별로였던 일을 해본 적 있어?

sentences.en: Oh yes. There's one in particular that I remember.
sentences.ko: 아, 있지. 특히 기억나는 게 하나 있어.

sentences.en: Ooh, that's intriguing.
I'm sure we're going to hear about it a bit later because that's what we're talking about today in Real Easy English – bad or difficult jobs we've had.
sentences.ko: 조금 있다가 듣게 되겠지. 오늘 Real Easy English에서 우리가 해봤던 별로였거나 힘들었던 일에 대해 이야기할 거니까.

sentences.en: Yes, and people should remember that they can get a free worksheet for this podcast at bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: 맞아, 그리고 이 팟캐스트의 무료 워크시트를 bbclearningenglish.com에서 받을 수 있다는 것도 기억해 주세요.

sentences.en: That's right.
So Neil, tell us all about your bad or difficult job.
sentences.ko: 그럼 닐, 그 별로였던, 힘들었던 일에 대해 전부 얘기해 줘.

sentences.en: Well, what happened was I found a job picking beans on a student holiday while I was in Canada.
sentences.ko: 음, 어떻게 된 거냐면, 캐나다에 있을 때 학생 방학 동안 콩 따는 일을 구했어.

sentences.en: Ooh. On a farm?
Yeah, but we had to travel a long way.
sentences.ko: 응, 그런데 엄청 멀리까지 가야 했어.

sentences.en: And when we got there, we discovered that you got paid by the amount that you picked.
sentences.ko: 그리고 도착해서 보니까, 딴 양만큼 돈을 받는 거였어.

sentences.en: OK.
And it cost $10 to get to this place on the coach and we worked really hard all day.
sentences.ko: 그곳까지 버스 타고 가는 데 10달러가 들었는데, 하루 종일 정말 열심히 일했어.

sentences.en: And then I got my beans and weighed them.
sentences.ko: 그다음에 딴 콩을 가져가서 무게를 쟀지.

sentences.en: And I got paid $8.
Oh wow.
Was it a full day's work?
Oh yeah. Hard, hard work in the heat, in a field.
sentences.ko: 그럼. 더위 속에서 밭에서 정말, 정말 힘들게 일했어.

sentences.en: Was it fun, at least?
Were you with friends?
It's a good story now...
OK.
...but at the time, it was very annoying.
Exhausting, it sounds.
It was exhausting.
All day in the heat.
I had quite a difficult job – it was just a temporary one.
sentences.ko: 나는 꽤 힘든 일을 했었어. 그냥 임시직이었지만.

sentences.en: I was working in customer service, so I had to pick up calls from customers who were needing help or were unhappy about the service they had.
sentences.ko: 고객 서비스 일을 했는데, 도움이 필요하거나 받은 서비스에 불만이 있는 고객들의 전화를 받아야 했어.

sentences.en: OK. That sounds interesting.
What didn't you like about this job?
Well, the company was having a difficult time, so many or most of the customers that were calling were unhappy about the service, and so I had to talk to people who were very angry,
sentences.ko: 음, 회사가 힘든 시기를 겪고 있어서, 전화하는 고객들 대부분이 서비스에 불만이 있었어. 그래서 아주 화난 사람들이랑 얘기해야 했는데,

sentences.en: and it felt like they were angry with me, even though it wasn't my fault.
sentences.ko: 내 잘못이 아닌데도 나한테 화를 내는 것처럼 느껴졌어.

sentences.en: The company changed the warehouse where they kept the products and the delivery company at the same time, so it was just all a big mess and I found it really stressful.
sentences.ko: 회사가 제품을 보관하는 창고와 배송 회사를 동시에 바꿔서 전부 엉망진창이었고, 나는 그게 정말 스트레스였어.

sentences.en: Yeah, you say stressful.
How else did it make you feel?
It made me feel very anxious because I took it too personally.
Like I said, it felt like they were angry with me, even though I had nothing to do with it.
sentences.ko: 말했듯이, 나랑은 아무 상관이 없는데도 나한테 화를 내는 것처럼 느껴졌거든.

sentences.en: If you heard somebody else talking about this kind of job, what advice would you give them?
sentences.ko: 누가 이런 일을 한다는 얘기를 들으면, 어떤 조언을 해주고 싶어?

sentences.en: Ooh, I would say, don't take it to heart.
sentences.ko: 음, 마음에 담아두지 말라고 할 거야.

sentences.en: As I said, I was taking it too personally, but you need to realise that you can only do your best.
sentences.ko: 말했듯이 나는 너무 개인적으로 받아들였는데, 내가 할 수 있는 건 최선을 다하는 것뿐이라는 걸 깨달아야 해.

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, you can go home and enjoy yourself, relax, and tomorrow is a new day.
sentences.ko: 그리고 결국 하루가 끝나면 집에 가서 즐기고 쉴 수 있고, 내일은 새로운 날이니까.

sentences.en: That's a very positive attitude.
Yes.
What advice would you give to people doing the job that you had in Canada?
sentences.ko: 네가 캐나다에서 했던 일을 하는 사람들에게는 어떤 조언을 해주고 싶어?

sentences.en: I think it's really important to do some research before you say yes to a job, if you're lucky to be able to choose.
sentences.ko: 운 좋게 일을 고를 수 있다면, 일을 수락하기 전에 조사를 좀 해보는 게 정말 중요한 것 같아.

sentences.en: So, probably find out how much you're going to get paid, what it means, and how much you have to pay to get to the place to do the job.
sentences.ko: 그러니까 돈을 얼마나 받는지, 그게 무슨 뜻인지, 일하러 가는 데 얼마가 드는지 알아보는 거지.

sentences.en: Yeah, that's very important.
And that's some good advice.
OK. So, let's recap the vocabulary that we used in the conversation.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 그럼 대화에서 쓴 어휘를 복습해 보자.

sentences.en: Good idea.
We had a few adjectives to describe work.
sentences.ko: 일을 묘사하는 형용사가 몇 개 나왔지.

sentences.en: You said that your job was stressful.
I did. So, you can describe something as 'stressful', and the emotion that you feel is 'stressed'.
sentences.ko: 맞아. 어떤 것을 'stressful'하다고 묘사할 수 있고, 그때 느끼는 감정은 'stressed'야.

sentences.en: You said that your job was exhausting, so it was very hard work, so you got very tired doing it.
sentences.ko: 너는 네 일이 'exhausting'했다고 했지. 정말 힘든 일이라서 하다 보면 엄청 피곤해졌다는 거야.

sentences.en: That's 'exhausting' and the feeling is 'exhausted'.
Yeah. And I think I also said my job was annoying.
sentences.ko: 응. 그리고 내 일이 'annoying'했다고도 말한 것 같아.

sentences.en: Yes.
And if something is annoying, it makes you feel annoyed.
Yes, that's right. I also used the expression 'take something personally', which is when you feel that someone is angry with you when they're actually angry at the situation.
sentences.ko: 맞아. 나는 'take something personally'라는 표현도 썼는데, 사실은 상황에 화가 난 건데 상대가 나한테 화를 낸다고 느끼는 거야.

sentences.en: Yeah. And you used another expression with a similar meaning – 'take something to heart'.
sentences.ko: 응. 그리고 비슷한 뜻의 다른 표현도 썼지. 'take something to heart'.

sentences.en: If you take something to heart, just as you explained, you feel bad.
sentences.ko: 'take something to heart'하면, 네가 설명한 것처럼 기분이 나빠지는 거야.

sentences.en: You feel someone is attacking you, but it's just the job.
sentences.ko: 누가 나를 공격한다고 느끼지만, 그냥 일일 뿐인 거지.

sentences.en: OK. Well, that is the end of this episode of Real Easy English, but Neil we'll be back next week, won't we?
sentences.ko: 좋아. 이번 Real Easy English는 여기서 끝인데, 닐, 다음 주에 돌아오지?

sentences.en: We will. Thank you for listening and goodbye.
Goodbye!
